entradas.text: After a long day at the palace, I was finally home. I thanked Serge and walked through the front gates, nodding at the two guards as I went by.
“Deana, what did I tell you? No running in the house.”
“All right, all right.”
“Papa! You're home!”
Even as I turned the doorknob, I could hear Deana rushing down the stairs to greet me.
"There's my beautiful princess!”
entradas.menu: "There's my beautiful princess!”

entradas.text: "There's my bright little daughter!"
entradas.menu: "There's my bright little daughter!"

entradas.text: I lifted Deana up and hugged her while trying to put the keys in the tray next to the entrance.
entradas.menu: Lift and hug her.

entradas.text: I lifted Deana up and hugged her while trying to put the keys in the tray next to the entrance.
She was growing fast. Lifting her up was no longer as easy as it once was.
“How was school?”
entradas.menu: “How was school?”

entradas.text: “Where is your mother?”
entradas.menu: “Where is your mother?”

entradas.text: “Oof! That's enough of that. You're a big girl now!”
entradas.menu: “Oof! That's enough of that. You're a big girl now!”

entradas.text: She started laughing.
“That's right! I'm a big girl now!”
I put her down and her expression turned serious.
"Boring. I liked my old school better."
“Mama's in the kitchen making dinner."
Monica appeared next to the kitchen door. She was wearing an apron and holding a spatula in her hand.
“Yes, Mama.”
Monica approached me and kissed me on the cheek. A tantalizing smell wafted from the kitchen behind her.
“Darling, you shouldn't have. What do we have a cook for?"
entradas.menu: “Darling, you shouldn't have. What do we have a cook for?"

entradas.text: “How was your day, dear?”
entradas.menu: “How was your day, dear?”

entradas.text: “Mmm, I'm hungry! When's dinner?”
entradas.menu: “Mmm, I'm hungry! When's dinner?”

entradas.text: “Terrific. I finally got to do some grocery shopping, just like old times. And I'm making your favorite.”
“I felt like going grocery shopping, just like old times. And besides, she can't make your favorite like I can."
“Hello to you too, Anton. It's almost done. I'm making your favorite.”
Zabla was one of my hometown's specialties -- a chickpea stew topped with beef braised in tomatoes and Bergian spices, traditionally served in a clay pot.
It was absolutely my favorite dish -- especially paired with Kebij, a potent unfiltered wine from my region.
“Mmm. It's my lucky day. What's the occasion?”
entradas.menu: “Mmm. It's my lucky day. What's the occasion?”

entradas.text: "Where's the Kebij?"
entradas.menu: "Where's the Kebij?"

entradas.text: I kissed Monica on the cheek.
entradas.menu: Kiss her on the cheek.

entradas.text: “No occasion. I just wanted to cheer everyone up a bit."
“Especially after what happened at the ball.”
"What, you and Petr didn't booze it up enough back at the palace?"
Her smile faded, and she lowered her voice so that Deana wouldn't hear.
“I am worried, Anton. For you, for the children -- and for the country."
Deana suddenly appeared next to us.
“Mama.”
“Yes, sweetheart?”
“I'm hungry!”
“We'll eat in just a minute. Will you help me set the table?”
“Anton, can you tell Franc to come down for dinner? He's been sulking in his room all day.”
Monica started taking out the plates while I headed upstairs to fetch my son.
Loud rock 'n' roll music echoed down the hallway from his room. I caught a faint hint of cigarette smoke.
I knocked on the door.
entradas.menu: Knock on the door.

entradas.text: I tried to open the door.
entradas.menu: Open the door.

entradas.text: The door was locked.
There was no response.
I knocked on the door.
entradas.menu: Knock on the door.

entradas.text: There was no response.
I tried to open the door.
entradas.menu: Open the door.

entradas.text: The door was locked.
“Franc, turn down that racket and open the door!”
entradas.menu: “Franc, turn down that racket and open the door!”

entradas.text: The stereo in Franc's room clicked off.
I knocked on the door again.
entradas.menu: Knock on the door again.

entradas.text: There was still no response.
He unlocked and opened the door.
“What do you want?”
“Dinner's ready.”
entradas.menu: “Food is ready.”

entradas.text: "Hand over those cigarettes and join your family for dinner.”
entradas.menu: "Hand over those cigarettes and join your family for dinner.”

entradas.text: “You smoke, don't you? I'm old enough to do what I want!"
“I am your father and you will respond when I ask for you!”
entradas.menu: “I am your father and you will respond when I ask for you!”

entradas.text: “Sorry, Dad -- I mean, Father. It won't happen again.”
“Great. I'm starving.”
Franc headed downstairs to the dining room and I followed after.
The table was prepared and Monica was ladling food onto the plates.
“Come on. Have a seat. It won't be as tasty if it's cold.”
As we started eating, the room went quiet. Monica's cooking was as delicious as ever, but I had the feeling that wasn't the reason nobody spoke.
Monica was the first to break the silence.
Franc suddenly slammed his hands on the table, rattling the plates. Monica, Deana and I stared at him.
“So, this is how it's going to be? We're just going to sit here like nothing happened?"
"Dad, you could have been killed. Mom could have been killed. Any one of us could have died!"
“And what would you have us do?”
entradas.menu: “And what would you have us do?”

entradas.text: “And yet, we are all still alive.”
entradas.menu: “And yet, we are all still alive.”

entradas.text: “You will not raise your voice to me, young man.”
entradas.menu: “You will not raise your voice to me, young man.”

entradas.text: “I don't know. Talk about it. Maybe.”
Deana's lower lip started trembling. Monica put her hand on Franc's shoulder.
“For now. But how long until this happens again?”
“But it's the truth!”
Franc got up from his seat.
"You don't care! You don't care what happens to me or Deana or anyone else--"
“Franc, honey, we can talk about this--”
“No, it's too late! Ugh, I hate this family."
He stormed out of the dining room. Deana started crying. Monica soothed her for a bit, then plopped her in front of the living room TV and returned to the table.
I opened the door and there she was, standing in front of me with expectant eyes.
“Say, did you know that they refurbished the grocery store?”
“I don't know if you remember the owner -- he's been there every day for the past 30 years.”
“Can you imagine doing the same job for so long? What if you were president for 20 years, for example?”
“Honestly, would that really be so bad?"
entradas.menu: “Honestly, would that really be so bad?"

entradas.text: “I don't want this country to suffer under another Soll.”
entradas.menu: “I don't want this country to suffer under another Soll.”

entradas.text: “20 years of this? I'd be dead!"
entradas.menu: “20 years of this? I'd be dead!"

entradas.text: “Anyway, the grocer really is a nice person. He threw in some extra vegetables with my--"
Monica measured me with her eyes for a moment.
“Agreed. That must never happen again.”
“Franc, sit down. Now!"
entradas.menu: “Franc, sit down. Now!”

entradas.text: "Fine, let's talk about it. Sit down.”
entradas.menu: “Fine, let's talk about it. Sit down.”

entradas.text: “Franc. Where are you going?”
entradas.menu: “Franc. Where are you going?”

entradas.text: “I'm going back to my room.”
“You'd waste your mother's delicious cooking?”
entradas.menu: “You'd waste your mother's delicious cooking?”

entradas.text: “You are going nowhere.”
entradas.menu: “You are going nowhere.”

entradas.text: "Go, then. And don't even think about coming out until you've learned to show some respect!"
entradas.menu: "Go, then. And don't even think about coming out until you've learned to show some respect!"

entradas.text: “I'm not hungry.”
“Alright. Sit back down. Let's talk.”
entradas.menu: “Alright. Sit down. Let's talk.”

entradas.text: Franc took his seat again, scowling.
“Whatever. Do as you like.”
entradas.menu: "Whatever. Do as you like."

entradas.text: “Don't worry. We are going to be fine.”
entradas.menu: “Don't worry. We are going to be fine.”

entradas.text: “Do you think I would let us go down so easily?”
entradas.menu: “Do you think I would let us go down so easily?”

entradas.text: “I know it was a close call, but everything is under control.”
entradas.menu: “I know it was a close call, but everything is under control.”

entradas.text: “How? How is it under control?”
“You don't need to know the details.”
entradas.menu: “You don't need to know the details.”

entradas.text: “My security assured me that they took all the necessary steps.”
entradas.menu: “My security assured me that they took all the necessary steps.”

entradas.text: “It was one rogue shooter. We were not even the target.”
entradas.menu: “It was one rogue shooter. We were not even the target.”

entradas.text: “The same security that let a person get shot in front of the palace?”
“No! It's always like this.”
“But what if we were?”
Franc smirked.
“No.”
“But it's not up to you, is it?”
“How are we possibly going to be fine?”
“Just trust me.”
entradas.menu: “Just trust me.”

entradas.text: He sighed.
Monica turned to me.
“Franc. Listen to your father. If your father says we don't need to worry, then we don't need to worry.”
“You have to trust him.”
“We all have to trust each other.”
Things calmed down a bit at the table. We finished our food in silence.
Time would tell.
Had I been lying to Franc and Deana? Was the threat to my family truly over?
I sat alone at the table and drained my glass of Kebij.
Franc got up first and retreated back to his room. Monica lifted Deana up and plopped her in front of the living room TV before returning to the table.
She sat down across from me.
“I promise if there truly is any threat to this family, you will be the first to know.”
entradas.menu: “I promise if there truly is any threat to this family, you will be the first to know.”

entradas.text: “All you need to worry about is putting more delicious dinner on our table.”
entradas.menu: “All you need to worry about is putting more delicious dinner on our table.”

entradas.text: “I worry too, Monica. Things might escalate.”
entradas.menu: “I worry too, Monica. Things might escalate.”

entradas.text: She got up, stood behind me and massaged my shoulders for a moment before leaving me alone in the dining room.
I banged on the door.
entradas.menu: Bang on the door.

entradas.text: “Why not? We could live like kings.”
entradas.menu: “Why not? We could live like kings.”

entradas.text: Monica measured me with her eyes for a moment.
“Franc. You know I would never let anything happen to you or Deana. Even if it costs me my life.”
entradas.menu: “Franc. You know I would never let anything happen to you or Deana. Even if it costs me my life.”

entradas.text: “I know, I know, but still...”
“Can you at least tell me if something's being done about this? It was real close, dad.”
"Papa, are the bad men gone?"
"It was only one bad man, Deana. And yes, he's gone now."
entradas.menu: "It was only one bad man, Deana. And yes, he's gone now."

entradas.text: "I will never let anyone hurt you, ever."
entradas.menu: "I will never let anyone hurt you, ever."

entradas.text: "Yes, your papa took care of everything!"
entradas.menu: "Yes, your papa took care of everything!"

entradas.text: "Okay, Papa."
Deana dashed down the hallway.
"Mama! Papa's here!"
"I just wanted to cheer everyone up a bit."
"Anyway, I just wanted to cheer everyone up a bit."
I realized my poor choice of words too late. Monica looked down at her plate.
“He's scared, Anton. And frankly, he isn't the only one.”
"You make plenty of rash decisions now, too. Franc's not the only one who's scared, Anton."
"He should feel lucky he has a father who cares about him. I never had that."
entradas.menu: "He should feel lucky he has a father who cares about him. I never had that."

entradas.text: "He's had every opportunity I never did. Why is he still acting out?"
entradas.menu: "He's had every opportunity I never did. Why is he still acting out?"

entradas.text: “Anton, he is still young.”
"I know. But there's not much longer we can shield him from the ugliness of the world."
entradas.menu: "I know. But there's not much longer we can shield him from the ugliness of the world."

entradas.text: "My father would've given me hell for that kind of insubordination."
entradas.menu: "My father would've given me hell for that kind of insubordination."

entradas.text: "That's what worries me. I made plenty of rash decisions when I was his age."
entradas.menu: "That's what worries me. I made plenty of rash decisions when I was his age."

entradas.text: Monica frowned at me and left to join Deana.
I could have lost my son back at the palace. Maybe he was right to be mad. Was the threat to my family truly over?
It was absolutely my favorite dish -- especially paired with Kebij, a potent unfiltered wine from Bergia.
“Turn those records up louder next time, won't you? I don't think the neighbors heard.”
entradas.menu: “Turn those records up louder next time, won't you? I don't think the neighbors heard.”

entradas.text: “Ha ha.”
"As long as you live in this house, you'll do as I command!”
entradas.menu: "As long as you live in this house, you'll do as I command!”

entradas.text: "I'm trying to quit that nasty habit. You ought to stop while you still can.”
entradas.menu: "I'm trying to quit that nasty habit. You ought to stop while you still can.”

entradas.text: "I'm just asking you to wait until you're out of the house.”
entradas.menu: "I'm just asking you to wait until you're out of the house.”

entradas.text: Franc heaved a sigh, handed me the packet and headed downstairs. I followed him to the living room.
"You mean --"
entradas.menu: "You mean --"

entradas.text: "Yes! Zabla!"
"Yes! Svabli!"
"Yes! Lorscha!"
Svabli was a classic Holsord delicacy -- vegetables and creamy sheep cheese sandwiched between thin layers of dough.
Lorscha was a Lachaven specialty usually reserved for special occasions -- a rich seafood stew with a heady garlic and paprika kick.
